strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: The Rust runtime owns a named headless run session advance and persists checkpoint state for the next caller.
The run session advance writes bounded HeadlessRunSessionAdvanced evidence and session checkpoint files without raw prompts, provider responses, files, commands, paths, or environment values.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting persistent_structured_ledger and Rust-owned execution authority.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.advance creates or advances a named run-control session, executes bounded existing continuation steps, persists a replay-safe checkpoint, and lets the next advance start from runtime-owned checkpoint evidence.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: headless.continue_once is request-scoped and requires callers to own session sequence, progress checkpoint handoff, continuation namespace construction, and lost-response replay.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: External schedulers or wrappers would still own long-running run-control state outside the Rust runtime.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M15.2 hardened AccessNetwork permission, M16.1 admitted verification retry tasks, and M16.2 ran targeted retry tasks; M17.1 adds session-level run control and checkpoint replay.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. A dedicated RPC is justified because the behavior owns persistent session sequence/checkpoint/replay state rather than a one-shot continuation request.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The result is tied to an actual advance attempt and persisted checkpoint, not a standalone status/report/readiness surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Valid calls execute existing continuation/task.run steps, write HeadlessRunSessionAdvanced evidence, persist session checkpoints, and replay an already committed advance without duplicate task execution.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can repeatedly advance a runtime-owned session from durable checkpoints instead of reconstructing raw progress state.
answers.milestone_progress: Establishes M17's first concrete run-control primitive while preserving explicit stop boundaries.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M17.1 updates the deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm actual run session checkpoint persistence and replay-safe execution, not a headless status wrapper.

exit_criteria: headless.run.advance accepts explicit authorization, session_id, expected_session_sequence, max_steps 1-3, and initial progress evidence for a new session
a valid new session advance executes bounded existing headless.continue_once/task.run steps
the runtime persists bounded session checkpoint evidence with start and post progress fingerprints
replaying the same session sequence returns the persisted checkpoint with replayed=true and no duplicate TaskRunning or HeadlessRunSessionAdvanced evidence
the next session sequence starts from the prior runtime-owned checkpoint without caller-supplied raw progress
stale initial progress and wrong session sequence fail before TaskRunning
existing headless.continue_once and direct task.run behavior remain compatible
no scheduler, background worker, automatic apply, automatic recovery, provider expansion, shell/git/network/service expansion, VSIX policy, or raw data exposure is introduced
next_phase_candidate_notes: After M17.1 merge, assess whether M17 needs bounded recovery for incomplete or conflicting session checkpoint writes. Do not add a dashboard/report/history phase.
